newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Africa protestors greet EU foreign ministers.
newsitem.headline: Africa protestors greet EU foreign ministers.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers gathering for their monthly meeting in Brussels on Monday were greeted by drum-beating protestors demonstrating for more positive EU action in Africa's Great Lakes region.

About two dozen protestors carried banners and handed out leaflets calling for the EU to take more decisive action in eastern Zaire, where thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees are trapped by fighting between rebels and government troops.
The Great Lakes is just one of the items on an agenda that includes trade links with South Africa and political ties with countries ranging from China to the United States.
They will also discuss the European Commission's latest proposals for laws relating to leg-hold traps used to capture animals for their fur.
At issue are standards for traps intended to kill or catch 18 species of wild animal -- including muskrat, beavers, sable, lynx and wolves.

Among more routine matters being discussed are relations with Mediterranean countries, former Yugoslavia, the situation in the Balkans and Albania, and a recent EU ministerial meeting with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

A planned discussion on human rights in China has been given extra relevance by the death last week of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and ministers are to debate whether to press -- possibly in collaboration with the U.S. -- for a motion to be raised at the United Nations.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat will also be in Brussels on Monday to sign an interim association agreement after which he will brief foreign ministers and Commission officials on the latest situation the the Middle East.
The agreement governs EU relations with the Palestinian entity and promises lucrative trade and other privileges for its exports.
